description.narrative: Global objective: Improved protection of relief personnel and improved effectiveness of humanitarian and development action Specific objective: Humanitarian and development organizations in Burkina Faso have access to timely, reliable, and high-quality safety services that help them plan, operate and deliver aid more safely. Expected Results: R1. Information, Analysis and Advice Credible, reliable, and high-quality safety information, analysis and advice is provided collectively to NGOs in a timely and appropriate manner. R2. Preparedness & Response - NGOs are supported in their own preparedness, security, and crisis management capacity.

Insatsen är ett institutionellt stöd ("core support") som syftar till att stärka kapaciteten hos den icke-statliga organisationen "International NGO Safety Organisation/INSO" i Burkina Faso för att ge information och utbildning till icke-statliga och icke vinstdrivande humanitära och utvecklingsorganisationer så att dessa kan arbeta med mindre risk och därmed mer effektivt i konfliktmiljöer. Att stödet är institutionellt innebär att INSO har större flexibilitet än normalt i att använda den svenska finansieringen för aktiviteter som saknar finansiering från andra givare men som är viktiga för att uppnå programmets mål.
Det totala finansiella stödet uppgår till 12 miljoner kr och ges under 3-årsperioden (aktivitetsperioden) 1 oktober 2020 - 30 september 2023.
Insatsens mål är som följer:
Utvecklingsmål: Förbättrat stöd till biståndspersonal och ökad effektivitet av humanitär hjälp och utvecklingsstöd.
Specifikt mål: Humanitära och utvecklingsorganisationer i Burkina Faso har tillgång till läglig, pålitlig och högkvalitativa tjänster som tillåter dem att planera och genomföra sina stödåtgärder på ett mindre riskfyllt sätt.

The initiative is an institutional support ("core support") aimed at strengthening the capacity of the non-governmental "International NGO Safety Organization / INSO" in Burkina Faso to provide information and training to non-governmental and non-profit humanitarian and development organizations so that these can work with less risk and thus more effectively in conflict environments. The institutional support can be used by INSO with more flexibility than usual in order to fund activities that lack funding from other donors but are essential for achieving the program's objectives.
The total financial support amounts to SEK 12 million and is given during the 3-year (activity) period 1 October 2020 - 30 September 2023.
The goals of the effort are as follows:
Global objective: Improved protection of relief personnel and improved effectiveness of humanitarian and development action
Specific objective: Humanitarian and development organizations in Burkina Faso have access to timely, reliable, and high-quality safety services that help them plan, operate and deliver aid more safely.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
INSO has successfully responded to increasing demands by expanding its operational scope and establishing additional regional offices.
Its broad presence in Burkina Faso and its leadership role in key humanitarian coordination forums underscore its operational strength. INSO is an active member of several key platforms, including the United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS) Steering Committee and the Access Working Group.
Over the course of the program, 189 humanitarian partners have benefited from INSO's information and analysis services. The organization consistently exceeded project targets and delivered significant results in both service delivery and capacity building.
The latest NGO user satisfaction survey (2024) highlights continued trust and appreciation for INSOs services, with a global satisfaction rate of 99.02%, matching the high satisfaction seen in 2023.
Goal 1 Information, Analysis and Advice
Concerning the Security Information and analysis Services:
INSO delivered 893 flash alerts and 705 updates, 455 security reports and 89 updates, published 196 weekly incident lists, 89 bi-weekly security reports, 13 quarterly reports and 28 regional analytical reports.
Concerning security coordination Meetings:
-1 153 safety roundtables were held during the entire project period with an average attendance of 15 participants. These meeting target NGO personell in charge of Security management. -49 country director monthly meetings were organized during the project period with an average attendance of 30 participants. -45 orientation briefings were delivered during the implementation period. INSO estimates the attendance to around 10 person per session, ie in total 450 participants. INSO's orientation breifing are being held monthly to newly arrived expatrates staff in Burkina Faso.
Concerning Independent security Advice (on-demand services)
INSO delivered during the implementation period 1253 on demand services (412 delivered in 2024 compared to 218 in 2023).
According to the evaluation survey conducted by INSO, the flash alerts and on demand services are the most appreciated service by partner NGO, supporting them in the daily planning of field missions.
Goal 2 prepardness and response
This result concerns the training component, which includes various modules on NGO security management, crisis management, Hostile environment individual safety training and Hostile environment First- aid-Training, field travel safety and humanitarian negotiations.
INSO delivered 202 training sessions over the complete intervention period, and in these, 2,534 aid workers were trained. (In 2024, 24 security trainings were carried out with a participation of 625 humanitarian staff including 170 women (27%). During 2024 INSO delivered a new course "Essentials of Humanitarian Access" (EHA), reaching 16 participants, with very good response from participants. An impact study, conducted in September 2024 on the training the trainer program, found that the train the trainer approach is an efficient capacity-building tool in humanitarian security management.
On-demand advisory services have had a notable increase in request for security assessments, briefings and situational analysis. This shows that INSO is trusted among its partners and valuable expertise.
INSO's membership base has increased across the years, the NNGO has increased from 2021 (17) to 2024 (29) NNGO, which is an important result as these organisations have the most risks as front-line actors.
